correctness.rationale: For s>1 choose a=b=p for any prime p|s, forcing both coordinates divisible by p. For s=1 write S(Y)=T(0,Y). If S is nonzero, bS(b)+1 has unbounded absolute value over positive b, so choose b with a prime divisor p and a=p>=2; modulo p both coordinates vanish. Therefore S=0 and X|T. Conversely for T=XU and all required inputs, positivity implies integer u=U(a,b)>=1. Setting m=abu gives (a^2u)(b^2u)=(m+1)(m-1)+1, an explicit nonnegative witness of gcd 1 (and cop predicate). Nonzero U forces X-degree(XT)>=2, attained T=X. The semiring weak-arithmetic corollary is restricted to nonnegative-coefficient T; the mixed-sign polynomial assertion is only standard integer truth. Independently verified symbolic Bezout identity and modular obstruction examples.
